title: Vesper and the Will
premise: Isandro Ishikawa, host of the true-crime podcast 'Vesper and the Will,' has spent three years documenting the 1997 disappearance of town matriarch Cordelia Vesper without ever accusing anyone. When twin letters arrive—one confessing to her murder, the other promising 'more if you keep listening'—Isandro is pulled from observer to participant. Following clues hidden in Cordelia's publicly displayed family ledger, they uncover a decades-long extortion scheme run by the town's founding families, who drowned Cordelia's fortune and her body in the tidal flats. The confessor is Cordelia's nurse, dying and guilt-ridden; the second letter's sender is the town's beloved sheriff, who wants Isandro silenced. In the climax at the tide flats, the ledger's final page surfaces with the body, exposing the sheriff, who is arrested as the town reckons with what justice outside a courtroom looks like—and Isandro broadcasts the truth they once only filed away.
about_author: Astrid Montrose is the pen name of a former coastal-town journalist who spent a decade covering cold cases before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about small places that keep large secrets, drawing on her obsession with archives, tide charts, and the things families agree never to say aloud.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Three years into the podcast, Isandro files the latest dead-end tip on Cordelia Vesper's disappearance and reflects on how safely distant the case has stayed. The emotional beat is the quiet vanity of the archivist—control mistaken for understanding—just before the first envelope arrives.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Two letters arrive the same morning: one a detailed confession to Cordelia's murder, the second promising 'more if you keep listening,' written in the same hand. Isandro's producer urges them to broadcast; Isandro hesitates. The beat is the collapse of safe distance—the observer suddenly observed.

chapters.title: The Nurse Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with a flashback. Isandro traces the confession's phrasing to Edith Marlowe, Cordelia's live-in nurse, now terminally ill in a hospice up the coast. Edith neither confirms nor denies. The beat is dread braided with tenderness—Isandro recognizing a person, not just a source.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Re-examining Cordelia's family ledger, displayed for decades in the town historical society, Isandro notices entries that don't balance—payments coded as garden expenses. The beat is the thrill of the hunt curdling into suspicion: someone curated this display on purpose.

chapters.title: What the Sheriff Remembers
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dale Pruitt's POV. Pruitt, a boy in 1997, recalls the night Cordelia vanished and his father's role in the search that found nothing. He learns a podcaster has been asking questions. The beat is polished public warmth over private alarm; the reader sees his mask before Isandro does.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Promise
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A third letter arrives: coordinates to the tidal flats and a warning that Edith will 'confess to the wrong crime' if Isandro goes to the sheriff. Isandro must choose between the law and the story. The beat is loyalty vs. truth beginning its long argument.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the flats at low tide, Isandro finds nothing but a rusted garden trowel—matching a ledger entry. Someone watches from the dune road. The beat is exhilaration shadowed by the first real fear: the sender knows Isandro's habits.

chapters.title: Edith's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Edith Marlowe's POV. In hospice, Edith recounts the coded ledger entries she helped Cordelia keep—records of blackmail paid by the founding families. She confesses she stayed silent for money for her sister's care. The beat is guilt as a slow tide, and love as its excuse.

chapters.title: Founding Families, Founding Sins
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro maps the ledger payers to the town's four dynasties—two still powerful, one extinct, one being the Pruitts. The podcast's research board becomes a target. The beat is the corruption of inherited power: everyone's grandfather was someone's victim.

chapters.title: A Visit from the Law
chapters.summary: Sheriff Pruitt's POV. Pruitt visits Isandro with coffee and warnings about 'stirring grief,' offering official access in exchange for editorial review. Isandro politely declines. The beat is a duel conducted entirely in courtesies; both leave knowing the other knows.

chapters.title: The Episode That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Producer Ren's POV. Ren secretly drafts an explosive episode from Isandro's files; when Isandro kills it, their partnership fractures. Ren leaks a fragment anyway. The beat is betrayal inside loyalty—the truth weaponized by someone who wants it told badly.

chapters.title: Fire in the Archive
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The historical society's ledger display is destroyed in a suspicious fire; the original ledger survives only because Isandro photographed it weeks earlier. The beat is grief for the town's shared memory and certainty that the arsonist is protecting, not hiding, something.

chapters.title: The Wrong Crime
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith, pressured by an unidentified visitor, prepares to confess to a manslaughter she didn't commit to close the case forever. She leaves Isandro a voicemail cut short. The beat is terror in a frail body, and the horror of a confession being manufactured.

chapters.title: Hospice Watch
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Isandro reaches Edith before she signs anything and smuggles out her full account, recorded on a cassette from the podcast's early days. The beat is fierce protectiveness—Isandro choosing a person over a story for the first time.

chapters.title: Decoding Cordelia
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cross-referencing the ledger's garden entries with tide tables, Isandro realizes Cordelia scheduled her own blackmail drops by the moon—and predicted her own death in the final entry, dated the night she vanished. The beat is awe and heartbreak: the victim was the best detective in the book.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sheriff Pruitt's POV. Pruitt confronts his dying father, learns the family's payments continued long after 1997, and that his badge was bought with them. He burns his father's letters. The beat is a man realizing his entire identity is a cover story.

chapters.title: Ren's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ren's POV. The leaked fragment goes viral; Pruitt's office opens a performative investigation targeting Edith. Ren, horrified, brings everything to Isandro and offers to help finish it right. The beat is repentance—loyalty rebuilt on truth instead of ambition.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The decoded ledger points to a once-a-decade spring tide that will expose the flats' deepest channel—the one Cordelia's final entry marked. Isandro broadcasts a teaser: in three days, the tide gives up what it took. The beat is the point of no return, publicly declared.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Isandro and Ren's POV, alternating. At the peak tide, before witnesses and cameras, the channel yields a strongbox: Cordelia's original ledger, her will, and evidence naming her killers. Pruitt arrives to stop it. The beat is triumph colliding with danger as the sheriff's composure finally cracks.

chapters.title: The Confession on the Flats
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Pruitt, cornered, confesses on a live feed—his father struck Cordelia during the final blackmail exchange; the family covered it; Pruitt buried the case to bury himself. Edith, listening from hospice by phone, forgives him aloud. The beat is devastating catharsis: justice spoken where the body lay.

chapters.title: After the Water Recedes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Arrests ripple through the founding families; the town splits between relief and resentment. Edith dies peacefully, her real confession aired with her consent. Isandro, exhausted, archives the case properly at last. The beat is the cost of truth—grief and gratitude in equal measure.

chapters.title: Vesper and the Will, Final Episode
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The last episode airs: Cordelia's voice restored through her ledger, her will funding the town archive she was denied in life. Isandro reads the final entry aloud and signs off, no longer invisible, no longer just filing secrets. The beat is quiet resolve—justice outside the law, but not outside the record.
